risks: Low for patients: minutes and treatment dates are used as recorded, and the package changes how decisions are written, not which treatment is given. The main risks are to staff (feeling judged) and to patients if longer meetings squeeze discussion time; both are monitored.
consent: Waiver of individual consent for minutes and treatment dates under approval REB-CN-2026-118; patients invited to the questionnaire give verbal or online consent and may decline without any effect on care.
data: Extracts are pseudonymised by the data manager; board and hospital identifiers are kept for the analysis; no clinician is named in any report; feedback reports go only to the board chair.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients with limited English or literacy, older patients and those from deprived areas are most at risk of mixed messages and least likely to complete questionnaires. The questionnaire is offered in four languages with help, results are reported by language and age group, and the template's patient-preference item is audited for these groups.
effectiveness: The trial shows whether the package improves documentation and patient-facing outcomes during a rollout that is happening anyway.
efficiency: Uses the rollout, existing coordinators and three data-manager days a month.
costs: No research budget beyond coordinator salaries already funded; questionnaire printing and translation from the network's patient experience budget.
grants: None needed for the trial; results may support a national case for coordinator posts.
partnerships: Board chairs, coordinators, the digital team, the patient representatives and the two merging hospitals' information teams.
rebPath: Approved by the research ethics board (REB-CN-2026-118) for an evaluation in which every board receives the template in 2027; the stepped-wedge design is within that approval, while the superseded parallel design with a December start was also within it but underpowered.
limitations: Few clusters; unblinded delivery; secular trends; the merger data gap.
summary: Waiver for routine data, consented questionnaire, equity reporting by language and age.
